verdicts.rationale: The introduction explicitly identifies rare CHD cohorts and normal-topology assumptions of prior generative methods as these challenges.
The pipeline includes diagnosis-conditioned implicit type representations, shape deformation, and correction of additional patient-specific topology variations.
The methods specify NODE-based invertible deformation and a 4×4×4×27 spatial shape-code grid.
The implementation explicitly trains with occupancy targets and extracts boundaries at the 0.5-level set.
The dataset description confirms CT images, diagnoses, seven-structure segmentations, expert-supervised processing, and the stated patient splits.
These are the six CHD types listed for the main dataset experiments; a separate experiment additionally introduces one single-ventricle example.
The assessment was blinded to generation diagnoses, used 50 random cases per method, and reported exactly these mismatch counts and predominant confusion.
The evaluation defines plausibility as maximum training-set Dice and reports higher means across 30 generated anatomies per type.
Table 4 reports all four whole-heart reconstruction values exactly as stated.
The experiment specifies 67 real and 420 synthetic images; Table 7 confirms both Dice changes and their significance markers.
The reported 3D UNet median VSD diameter and area percentage errors match the claim exactly.
The local-defect analysis attributes the missed apical VSD to subaortic-only templates and states that correction also failed.
The limitations explicitly describe the shared Gaussian prior as simplifying and acknowledge type-dependent distributions and limited samples.
Increasing latent spatial resolution improved unseen reconstruction but caused non-physiological synthetic shapes.
The discussion explicitly distinguishes reduced intersection artifacts from the absence of a positive-Jacobian guarantee.
The limitations report small-branch reconstruction difficulties for all methods and limited exploration of vessel-connection generation.
The stated contributions combine smooth implicit representations with diffeomorphic deformation and demonstrate both application classes.
